verdict.rationale: Keycloak's own docs cover each part of the story. Client-credentials service accounts give each client (and so each agent) its own non-human identity (kc-supp-client-credentials), and dynamic client registration and the Admin CLI/REST API let you create these per agent (keycloak-docs-39, kc-supp-kcadm). Fine-grained, resource-level and role-based authorization narrows permissions, and a token revocation endpoint handles both access and refresh tokens (kc-supp-authz-services, keycloak-docs-49, keycloak-docs-70, keycloak-docs-53). missing for 10: agent-specific guidance or framing, explicit docs on narrowing token scopes per service account, evidence that revocation is instant for self-contained access tokens without introspection (keycloak-docs-52 offers introspection as a validation path), and independent hands-on corroboration of machine-identity use.
